title: Sandboxed burst experiments and autoscale operator QA notes
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures a lightweight PRD + experiment runbook for a sandboxed approach to validating autoscale operator changes and burst-handling policies for Dedicated capacity. Focus is on safe experiments, operator-level QA checks, tenant isolation validation, and a small set of measurable success criteria before any rollout to production pools.

Context / why this now:
- We have many design drafts for autoscaling/burst options but limited operator QA coverage for regressions that only show up under spiky arrival patterns and mixed-tenant noise.
- Recent customer reports (customer-CS ticket JIRA-DDED-361) showed tail latency regressions during multi-tenant microbursts that standard unit tests didn't catch.
- Need a repeatable sandbox workflow to: (1) exercise autoscaler decisions, (2) validate isolation controls (soft-quarantine, per-tenant headroom), (3) measure cost and latency tradeoffs.

High-level goals (what success looks like):
- A stable experiment harness that can simulate 10x microburst traffic to a dedicated pool without cascading failures.
- Autoscaler operator must respect tenant-priority tags and apply soft-quarantine within 30s of policy trigger in sandbox mode.
- No more than 3% increase in p95 latency for protected tenants in the sandbox compared to baseline.
- A clear rollback signal and automated safeguards for runaway scaling (cost threshold or sustained queue growth).

User stories / personas:
- Platform SRE: needs diagnostics to debug when a tenant hits soft-quarantine and verify tracer flows.
- Solutions engineer: wants to test a customer's burst plan in a copy of their pool before recommending a commitment change.
- Product manager: needs a pass/fail checklist to greenlight gradual rollout of a new burst-delegate policy.

Constraints and non-goals:
- This is not the final autoscaler algorithm; it is an experimental validation layer and operator QA path.
- Sandbox will run on dedicated k8s nodes earmarked for experiments; not intended for long-term production traffic.

Functional requirements (sandbox + QA operator):
1) Sandbox environment provisioning:
   - Scripted creation of a dedicated sandbox pool that mirrors a real pool's topology (GPU types, VM sizes, zone).
   - Ability to clone tenant configs and metadata (priority tags, quotas) into the sandbox.
   - Toggle to run autoscaler in "operator-qa" mode where scale decisions are logged and optionally applied.

2) Synthetic workload generator:
   - Workload harness that can produce configurable arrival patterns: steady, ramp, sawtooth, poisson microbursts, and blended multi-tenant spikes.
   - Support tokenized prompt payloads and model kernels that match heavy transformer runs (long context + large batch).
   - Track per-tenant metrics (requests/sec, tokens/sec, queue depth, latency distribution).

3) Isolation policy tester:
   - Simulate policy triggers: hard cap, soft-quarantine, priority preemption, headroom borrowing.
   - Verify that operator applies isolation decisions (throttles, queue re-routing, fallback model selection) and records audit events.

4) Safety gates & aborts:
   - Configurable abort thresholds: cumulative cost run-rate, sustained p99 latency above threshold, queue growth > X seconds, error rate spike > Y%.
   - Upon abort, operator must: (a) stop synthetic load, (b) revert cluster to baseline config, (c) capture heap/profile/trace dumps, (d) notify on-call channel.

5) Telemetry and diagnostics:
   - Per-experiment telemetry export: autoscaler decisions timeline, allocation events, prewarm traces, KV cache hits, per-tenant token accounting.
   - Hooks to upload traces to the Console's per-route timelines for postmortem.

Nonfunctional requirements:
- Experiment runs should be reproducible and seedable.
- All logs and telemetry must be retained for at least 30 days for investigation.
- Experiment harness must limit cloud spend to a user-set budget.

Experiment matrix (first pass):
- Axis A: Arrival pattern (steady / 3x ramp / sudden 10x microburst / noisy multi-tenant spike)
- Axis B: Failure mode (none / slow disk / natting delay / preemption event)
- Axis C: Isolation policy variant (no isolation / soft-quarantine / hard cap with fallback / per-tenant headroom)
- Axis D: Autoscale operator mode (dry-run / apply / aggressive-prediction / conservative-threshold)
For each cell capture: p50/p95/p99 latencies, tokens/sec, number of scale events, time-to-scale, cost delta vs baseline, and audit-event logs.

Operator QA checklist (manual + automated checks):
- Sanity: sandbox pool created with same node labels and model payloads.
- Config: tenant metadata cloned and validated.
- Dry-run: observe autoscaler decisions for at least 3 burst cycles in dry-run mode.
- Apply-run: enable operator apply if dry-run looked stable and re-run selected scenarios.
- Isolation: ensure soft-quarantine reduces target tenant token throughput but leaves high-priority tenant unaffected.
- Rollback: intentionally trip abort threshold to validate automated rollback and data collection.
- Metrics: verify telemetry export to Console and that traces correlate with autoscaler events.

Operational runbook (short):
- Start: provision sandbox (tools/setup-sandbox.sh), seed cloned tenants (tools/clone-tenant.sh --source pool-prod-12).
- Run control: start harness (tools/simulate-burst --pattern microburst --tenants 20 --duration 600).
- Observe: tail logs (kubectl logs -f autoscaler-operator-qa) and the sandbox dashboard (Console -> experiments -> <id>).
- Abort: run tools/stop-experiment --id <id> or wait for automated abort. On abort, tag experiment with failure_reason and link traces.
- Post: collect core dumps and traces (tools/collect-artifacts.sh --exp <id>), notify SRE on Slack #dedicated-autoscale.

Sample small-scale test scenario (walkthrough):
1) Clone pool-prod-5 into sandbox-sim-09 with 4 nodes (same instance types).
2) Seed 3 tenants: gold (priority=high), silver (priority=medium), bronze (priority=low, noisy).
3) Run arrival: bronze emits 15 concurrent short requests for 90s (sustained burst), silver emits 2x steady load, gold steady low traffic.
4) Expected behavior: autoscaler should allocate transient worker slices for bronze but enforce headroom for gold; soft-quarantine applied to bronze if queue > 3s for > 20s.
5) Observations to capture: scale events timeline, bronze p95, gold p95 delta, audit logs of quarantine triggers, cost delta.

QA automation ideas (future work):
- Add a CI job that runs a 10-minute microburst simulation against the operator in an isolated cluster and fails PRs on regressions in p95 or decision logs.
- Build a lightweight golden-trace diffing tool that matches autoscaler decision sequences across runs.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- How conservative should the sandbox abort thresholds be relative to production? (We want safety but don't want to constantly abort experiments.)
- Do we accept some divergence between sandbox and prod model kernels for faster iteration (emulation) or must we always run the real model?
- Should the autoscaler dry-run recordings be compressed and stored long-term for ML-driven decision improvements?

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: synthetic harness causes accidental account-level quota exhaustion. Mitigation: budget guardrails, per-experiment IAM restricted role.
- Risk: operator behavior differs under multi-tenant network jitter. Mitigation: add failure-mode axis that injects jitter and test it early.

Next steps / action items (owners):
- Diego: prototype the sandbox provisioner (due 2024-09-20).
- Amina: implement the synthetic workload generator and add Poisson burst patterns (due 2024-09-30).
- Priya: draft the CI gating proposal and metrics thresholds (due 2024-10-07).
- Liam: wire telemetry export to Console experiment views (due 2024-10-04).

Appendix: quick links and shorthand notes:
- runbook scripts repo: github.com/redwood-inference/ops/experiment-scripts
- relevant tickets: JIRA-DDED-987 (autoscale proto), JIRA-DDED-361 (customer incident)
- slack threads: #dedicated-autoscale (pin: experiment-wg)

Notes to self: keep experiment names short, tag with customer-like ids, avoid running more than 3 large experiments concurrently in the same billing account.

-- end of draft --
